01 Trends: growth before and after 2019¶

The logic lives in pipeline/tract/growth.py. This notebook loads, calls and shows.

What "before" and "after" mean

  • ACS 5-year estimates describe a window, not a year. Windows: 2010-14, 2015-19, 2020-24. Midpoints: 2012, 2017, 2022
  • Before = 2010-14 to 2015-19 (about 2012 to 2017). After = 2015-19 to 2020-24 (about 2017 to 2022)
  • So the ACS "after" step starts two years before 2019. Read it as "the most recent 5 years", not "since 2019"
  • Jobs (LODES) are yearly counts: before = 2010 to 2019, after = 2019 to 2024
  • Yearly rate = (end / start) ^ (1 / 5) - 1 for ACS, over 9 or 5 years for jobs

Inputs: acs_tract.csv, acs_moe_tract.csv (margins, from python -m pipeline.tract.acs_moe), jobs_tract.csv, decennial_units_tract.csv, tracts_2020.gpkg, the 2010 to 2020 block crosswalk

Outputs: trends_tract.csv (the tool reads it), tract_panel.csv, processed/5500/growth_summary.json

Inflation¶

  • ACS dollars are in the last year of each window. CPI-U (tract.growth.cpi_u in shared/assumptions.json) moves them to 2024 dollars
  • Nominal median rent rose a lot. Real rent rose a little

Margins of error¶

  • ACS margins are at 90%. The margin of a difference between two windows is sqrt(m1^2 + m2^2)
  • A change smaller than its margin is flagged in trends_tract.csv (*_within_moe)
  • "change" = the change in the 5-year change (2020-24 minus twice 2015-19 plus 2010-14)

Interactive views¶

The same growth numbers, but you can explore them. Pick a measure, then drag a box on the scatter. The histogram shows how much the picked tracts sped up or slowed down after 2019. Points on the dashed line grew at the same pace in both periods.

In [2]:
import altair as alt
import geopandas as gpd

alt.renderers.enable("html")            # the chart works in the saved HTML page too
alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows()

t = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data/processed/trends_tract.csv", dtype={"GEOID": str})
parts = []
for m, name in [("jobs", "Jobs"), ("pop", "People"), ("units", "Homes"), ("rent", "Rent")]:
    d = t[["GEOID", f"{m}_growth_before", f"{m}_growth_after"]].dropna()
    d.columns = ["GEOID", "before", "after"]
    d["measure"] = name
    parts.append(d)
long = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)
long[["before", "after"]] = (long[["before", "after"]] * 100).clip(-10, 10).round(1)  # % a year, clipped for the axes
long = long.drop(columns="GEOID")   # keeps the page small

measure = alt.param(name="measure", value="Jobs",
                    bind=alt.binding_select(options=["Jobs", "People", "Homes", "Rent"], name="Measure "))
brush = alt.selection_interval(encodings=["x", "y"])
base = alt.Chart(long).transform_filter(alt.datum.measure == measure)

scatter = base.mark_circle(size=14, opacity=0.5).encode(
    x=alt.X("before:Q", title="% a year, before 2019"),
    y=alt.Y("after:Q", title="% a year, after 2019"),
    color=alt.condition(brush, alt.value("#2f746f"), alt.value("#d6d3d1")),
    tooltip=["before:Q", "after:Q"],
).add_params(measure, brush).properties(width=340, height=320, title="Each tract, before and after 2019")
same = alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"v": [-10, 10]})).mark_line(color="#94a3b8", strokeDash=[4, 4]).encode(x="v:Q", y="v:Q")

shift = base.transform_filter(brush).transform_calculate(shift="datum.after - datum.before").mark_bar(color="#2f746f").encode(
    x=alt.X("shift:Q", bin=alt.Bin(maxbins=40), title="After minus before (pts a year)"),
    y=alt.Y("count():Q", title="Tracts"),
).properties(width=300, height=320, title="Speed-up or slow-down of the picked tracts")

(scatter + same) | shift

A map you can zoom and hover (GeoPandas .explore(), which draws with folium and Leaflet). Job growth after 2019 per tract. Hover a tract for its people, jobs and rent growth. Tracts whose people change is inside the ACS margin of error say so in the label.

In [3]:
import shapely
import warnings

warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)   # shapely warns on a few tract rings while simplifying. The shapes are fine
g = gpd.read_file(ROOT / "data/processed/tracts_2020.gpkg")[["GEOID", "NAMELSAD", "geometry"]].to_crs(4326)
g["geometry"] = shapely.set_precision(g.geometry.make_valid().simplify(0.004, preserve_topology=True).values, 0.001)  # about 400 m: a small page
g = g.merge(t[["GEOID", "jobs_growth_after", "pop_growth_after", "rent_growth_after", "pop_after_within_moe"]], on="GEOID")
for c in ["jobs_growth_after", "pop_growth_after", "rent_growth_after"]:
    g[c] = (g[c] * 100).round(1)
g["people_moe"] = g.pop_after_within_moe.map({True: "inside margin of error", False: "clear change"})

g.drop(columns="pop_after_within_moe").explore(
    column="jobs_growth_after", cmap="RdYlGn", vmin=-5, vmax=5, tiles="Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",
    tooltip=["NAMELSAD", "jobs_growth_after", "pop_growth_after", "rent_growth_after", "people_moe"],
    tooltip_kwds={"aliases": ["Tract", "Jobs % a year", "People % a year", "Rent % a year", "People"]},
    style_kwds={"weight": 0.2, "color": "white", "fillOpacity": 0.75},
    legend_kwds={"caption": "Jobs, % a year after 2019"},
)
